results.corrected_extracted: Record of what the retracted report claimed, never evidence about MDMA (METHODS §3.2): squirrel monkeys and baboons given 2 mg/kg three times at 3-hour intervals (subcutaneously and intramuscularly), presented as modelling a regimen used at all-night dance parties. One squirrel monkey died of malignant hyperthermia and one baboon died after two doses, and in each species one further animal received only two doses, so 2 of 10 animals given the regimen died and 2 more did not complete it. The squirrel monkey that received two doses was reported at 6 weeks with caudate dopamine -65%, DOPAC -77% and dopamine transporter -51%, against serotonin -37%, 5-HIAA -48% and serotonin transporter -40%. The report concluded that people taking repeated doses over several hours risk severe dopaminergic injury and possible parkinsonism, either as young adults or later in life, and argued the doses were lower than human doses (1.6 to 2.4 mg/kg) after interspecies scaling.
